note: Disc golf course looks (D-117), presentation only - DiscCourse builds every basket, tee pad, tee sign and basket ring from these; a course picks its pieces in data/discgolf/courses.json "look" {basket, tee, sign, ring, wear 0..1}. Matched to the real Kearney courses (PDGA / UDisc / DGCourseReview): Centennial Park = Mach II-style baskets with a small landscaped mulch circle, big asphalt tee pads, one sign per hole; Cottonmill = newer two-tier chain baskets (the course was refitted with them), concrete tee pads, framed hole signs. wear = rust on the steel, faded sign paint, tilted posts (the world is post-apocalyptic). Baskets, metres above the base: pole_r / pole_top, the wire tray from tray_bottom to tray_top (radius tray_r, tray_bars uprights, hoops = heights of extra rings), the chain band (band_r, band_bottom..band_top, glows - D-076), spokes from the pole to the band, chain tiers {count, top_r at the band, bottom_r near the pole at bottom_y, sag outward, twist_deg round the pole}; near_m = drawn link by link (link: pitch, length, width, wire thickness) up to here, the simple version from there to far_m. Keep tray / chain heights in step with the catch zone in data/tuning/disc_golf.json (tray_low_m, chains_low_m, chains_high_m, catch_radius_m). Tees: pad size [width, length], texture from assets/textures, top_m above the ground. Signs: board [width, height] standing height_m up on 1 or 2 posts, colours; the face shows the hole number, par, length and a drawn map of the hole.
